content_sections.body: In clinic visit, put finished actions in a clear order. Use time words such as yesterday, first, then, and this morning. Example: “I felt ill yesterday.” The past action tells the listener what happened; the time word tells when.
content_sections.title: Notice the language

content_sections.body: I felt ill yesterday. The nurse asked two questions and gave me useful advice. Ask: what detail would a friend need next? Say the key action once, then add one time or place detail.
content_sections.title: Context and meaning

content_sections.body: Choose a true or invented clinic visit detail. Say two connected sentences: one about what happened and one about the next step. Check that the order is easy to follow.
content_sections.title: Guided use

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence that best reports the main event in this clinic visit situation.
Complete this sentence: Yesterday, I _____. Use the lesson 4 situation.
Read the short clinic visit message and answer: What problem or detail does the speaker mention?
Tell a partner about a clinic visit situation using two ordered sentences.
exercises.rubric: Reports a clear event.; Uses an understandable time or sequence word.; Answers one follow-up question.

objectives: Organize a short account in a clear event order.

constraints: Keep transcript private until the first answer.
Ask exactly one question before revealing it.
Use no media; use only the supplied transcript.
listening.goal: Catch the main event and one detail about clinic visit.
listening.instruction: Listen once to a short message about clinic visit. Answer one question before seeing the transcript. Then listen again and notice the sequence words.

pronunciation.goal: Make the event order and main action easy to hear.
pronunciation.instruction: Practise the concrete sound target for clinic visit: group the message into two thought groups and stress the main action word. Read the example slowly, then at natural speed.

constraints: Use at most three tutor turns.
Stop after agreeing on a next step.
speaking.goal: Complete a useful exchange about clinic visit.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a customer or friend dealing with clinic visit; the tutor is the staff member or friend who has one missing detail. Scenario: explain what happened and ask for the next step. Tutor opening: “Hi, what happened?” Ask one follow-up about time, place, quantity, or result; finish when the tutor understands and you agree on the next step.

constraints: Do not replace the learner draft.
writing.goal: Write a clear short message about clinic visit.
writing.instruction: Write 3 short sentences about clinic visit: say what happened, add when or where, and say what happened next. Submit your draft first.

title: A short personal account
